mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: matter is the same as its neighbouring term in this chapter, so the decision does not change.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: Objects and materials such as water, food, clothes, books, and air are treated as matter when they have mass and occupy space.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when Objects and materials such as water, food, clothes, books, and air are treated as matter when they have mass and occupy space is not true.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: Judge from the most visible feature in the figure, not from the mechanism's test.

intelligence.enrichment: Elements and compounds are building blocks of matter, and matter is everything that has mass and takes up space; light, heat, and electricity are not matter. Having mass and occupying space makes something matter, while forms such as light, heat, and electricity do not meet that matter criterion. The learner correctly applies this rule: Elements and compounds are building blocks of matter, and matter is everything that has mass and takes up space; light, heat, and electricity are not matter. Anything around us that we can sense is matter.
